subject: phoenix
reasoning:
I'm planning out a phoenix model for the SDK—a standing bird in rest pose with wings extended, a long feathered tail, crest, beak, and taloned legs, using a fiery red-orange-gold palette, sized around 1.2m tall with a 3m wingspan.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure: a root joint at the hips, a spine chain curving from pelvis to chest, a neck chain forming an S-curve up to the head, and a hinged jaw joint, then figuring out how to loft the body shape along these bone chains from tail base to head.

For the body, I'm defining width/height stations along the spine and neck bones, then coloring the sweep with a countershading paint that blends a deep red back into a gold belly, and planning to add feather scale detail across the chest.

For the head, I'm adding a sphere element plus a crest of backward-sweeping cone spikes, roughly five of them.

Now I'm shaping the beak with an upper jaw spike tapering to a point and a smaller lower jaw spike, along with simple sphere eyes placed on either side of the head.

For the wings, I'm building each arm as a joint chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist to tip, using polyline segments to connect the points on both sides symmetrically.

I'm sweeping each wing chain into tapering tube geometry, then planning feathers as flat extruded shapes fanning out from the wrist and hand, defining a reusable feather part function that extrudes an outline along the feather's length and width within the wing's roughly horizontal plane.

For the feather shapes, I'm using a leaf-like outline with a sharp tip and thin cross-section, keeping the color palette limited to around a dozen flat colors since there's a 64-color cap, applying a red-to-orange-to-gold progression by picking colors from that palette by index rather than using costly gradient paints.

I'm laying out primaries as a seven-feather fan from the hand/wrist outward with decreasing length, secondaries along the forearm pointing backward, and shorter covert rows in orange and gold over the arm with tertials near the body, keeping wings horizontal for the T-pose with slight y-offsets per row to avoid z-fighting, and attaching feathers to the shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand bone chain.

Checking the cross product for the thickness axis across left/right symmetry — the sign flips depending on side, but since makeBasis always builds a right-handed frame, the winding stays consistent regardless.

I'll skip adding a rachis down the center, but I'll add a two-tone effect: a slightly smaller, raised inner vane overlay in a gold color for each feather. That nearly doubles the part count across primaries, secondaries, and covert rows, pushing the total feather count into the dozens per wing.

For the tail, I'm planning long curved streaming feathers trailing back from the tail base, built as flat box-section sweeps along catmull-rom paths with tapering width, each angled slightly differently for a fanned look, tied to a tail bone chain.

Plotting the central tail feather path curving down and slightly back up near the tip, keeping it clear of the floor, with the feather's width tapering thin toward the end.

Setting fiery gradient bands from red to gold, then shaping the nine tail feathers with varying lateral spread and length for the side plumes.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry with digitigrade posture: hip positioned high, knee bent forward and hidden under feathers, ankle/hock swept back, then down to the ball of the foot before splitting into three forward toes plus a back hallux, building the leg chain as a polyline through these joints.

I'm setting the thigh sweep radii and color bands so the upper leg stays feathered red while transitioning to scaly gold-yellow below the knee, then sketching three angled toe sweeps extending from the foot with talon spikes at their tips.

Now I'm working out the toe rigging: each toe could be its own two-joint digit chain, with four toes per foot across both legs adding sixteen joints total, so I'm figuring out whether each toe path needs two spans via three points to represent a knuckle properly.

I'm settling on toe geometry with tapering radii, positioning joints so the feet touch the floor correctly, and planning talon spikes projecting downward from the toe tips.

Scattering small cone-shaped feather spikes across the chest surface, using scattered ray hits with minimum distance spacing for a plume-like effect.

Skipping the neck collar idea, I'll add a crest and neck mane using sweeps: five curved feather paths running from head back and up, tapered with a radius function, attached to the head bone, with the head itself modeled as a sphere positioned near the top of the skull.

For the neck I'm sweeping the body up to a narrower width where it meets the head sphere, which overlaps slightly for a seamless join. The beak is the trickier part -- I want the upper beak as a tall, curved cone-like sweep with a flattened cross-section tapering to a hooked point, built from a few curved guide points so it bends downward like a real beak, colored and bound to the head bone.

Now I'm working out the lower beak as a shorter, less curved sweep in a slightly darker orange, bound to the jaw, and adjusting the vertical centers and radii of both beak pieces so they meet cleanly at a closed mouth line without ugly overlap. I'm also placing the jaw and head joints with their positions, directions, and parent bone relationships so the rig connects properly to the neck chain.

I'm then figuring out the neck catmull points and confirming the start matches the spine chain's end point, defining the spine and neck joint names and spans, and resolving the ambiguous parenting at the spine2/neck junction by explicitly assigning parents for each chain (spine to root, neck to spine2, tail and legs to root, wings to spine2). Now I'm setting the shoulder coordinates for the wing attachment point relative to the body.

I'm now laying out the arm skeleton for the wing, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand-tip points to form a 3-span polyline with tapering sweep radii and a red leading-edge covert, then working out how to distribute nine primary feathers along the hand section with varying base positions, angles, and lengths from outer to inner.

Checking the total wingspan, I realize the proportions are too large relative to the body, so I'm scaling down the arm segments and recalculating elbow, wrist, and hand coordinates to bring the span closer to a more believable size. I'm also positioning the nine secondary feathers along the elbow-to-wrist span, angling them mostly backward and slightly outward with lengths tapering from near the wrist toward the body.

Writing feather layout code...

So primaries anchor to the wrist joint since the hand tip is just an endpoint. Now I'm defining a feather helper function that extrudes a feather outline from a base point along a direction vector, with parameters for length, width, color, thickness, and the owning bone.

I'm working out the perpendicular width direction for each feather by projecting the vertical axis onto the plane orthogonal to the feather's direction vector, being careful since the secondaries point nearly straight back along z and the projection could get flattened if not handled carefully.

Defining the leaf outline shape...

I'm defining a layered feather function that scales length and width across three overlapping layers with staggered offsets, baking in a bone chain for the body loft so the mesh deforms correctly along the spine and neck.

For texture I'm scattering small cone-shaped stick feathers across the body surface using raycasts to find valid spawn points, filtering by position and normal direction, and cycling through colors—though I realize the cones point straight out radially, which looks too spiky, so I need to flatten them and angle them to flow more naturally like real feathers.

To fix this, I'm pre-transforming the shared cone geometry before instancing: translating so the base sits at the origin, scaling along one axis to flatten it into a feather-like shape, then rotating around X so it leans backward along the flow direction rather than sticking straight out, reusing this single geometry across all the scattered sticks for efficiency.

Now I'm placing the eyes and head: white sclera spheres with black pupils positioned just outside the scaled head sphere's surface, plus a gold-orange skin tone for the head itself with a small cheek patch for color variation.

For the crest, I'm setting up five feather plumes attached near the head joint, each defined by curved start/mid/end points with the center plume longest and outer ones shorter and angled outward, reusing the tail's ribbon-generation approach for tapered, flattened feather shapes.

With the up vector set this way, the ribbon stays thin along the vertical axis, giving a horizontal spread good for a tail, while color bands split into red, orange, and gold zones along the length. I'm now thinking about using nine tail feathers with varying widths.

For the central streamers I want two longer feathers with a wider max width, and I'm setting up a tail joint chain built from a Catmull-Rom curve through four control points, giving three spans named tail1 through tail3. I plan to skin the feather ribbons to this chain using closest-point binding along the whole tail path rather than a single rigid bone, so the motion flows smoothly even for off-center feathers.

Checking proportions now: crest height around 1.8, wingspan near 4.2, and tail ribbons dipping to y 0.22 while wings sit around y 1.1, all consistent. I'm also adding orange pantaloon feathers as scaled ellipsoids at the hips, and mapping out toe placement so the ball of the foot and leg sweep stay just above floor level before building the toe polyline chains.

Writing toe joint logic...

For the wing chain I'll use a 4-point polyline through shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand, giving 3 spans and naming all 4 joints down to the tip, parenting the wing shoulder explicitly to spine2.

Setting up the joint hierarchy now: root as the base, then spine chain built with catmull-spline points (3 points, 2 spans) parented to root with spine1/spine2 names, followed by a neck chain similarly parented to spine2, then a head joint positioned and oriented off neck2, leading next into the jaw joint.

Adding the jaw joint off the head, then building leg chains with hip/knee/ankle/foot joints per side using polyline points parented to root, followed by sweeping the leg with tapering radii and color bands along the chain.

Now I'm sketching the wing arm sweep with its own tapering radii and red coloring, then starting the actual build script defining the phoenix structure. For texturing, I'm setting up scale patterns for the back (reds/oranges) and belly (yellows/oranges) to countershade the body.
